Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: He's had glue ear a few times, which has affected his hearing temporarily. We've taken him to the doctor each time it happens and they've helped clear it up.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: His front teeth are larger than usual, and the dentist has mentioned keeping an eye on them to ensure they don't cause any further issues with his bite or speech.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: He gets tired easily when playing with friends or running around. The doctor said it might be related to his heart not being as efficient as it should be, but we need more tests to understand it fully.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).

Parent: Apart from what we've discussed, our son moves a bit differently compared to his peers. He also has scoliosis, which affects his posture and requires regular exercises to help improve it.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tiredness easily when engaging in physical activities, which may be related to an inefficient heart. Further tests are required to understand this fully.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes. Some may require surgery, while others only need monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences bowel problems that can be unpredictable. Establishing a routine has helped minimize these issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding. A lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tethered cord issue, which has caused concerns about his movement and coordination. He also has scoliosis, affecting his posture and requiring regular exercises.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments. Some may have difficulties with developmental delay and learning disabilities.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had glue ear, which has temporarily affected his hearing. He has also had issues with his teeth, including larger than usual front teeth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss. Many children require multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, requiring special glasses to correct his vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint. Treatment can include patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has larger than usual front teeth, which the dentist is monitoring to prevent further issues with his bite or speech.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome experience dental concerns, including weak enamel, requiring careful brushing and regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically require extra help in school, with some attending mainstream primary school and others requiring special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's movement and coordination seem a bit off compared to his peers, and he has scoliosis.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often experience developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has scoliosis, which affects his posture and requires regular exercises.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, leading to increased curvature of the spine. Others may experience short fingers, curved fingers, or hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor the patient's teeth and prevent further issues.
* Regular hearing reviews to ensure the patient's hearing is not further affected by glue ear or other conditions.
* Eyesight review to monitor the patient's vision and adjust his glasses as necessary.
* Cardiac review to further investigate the patient's heart condition and determine the best course of treatment.
* Referral for a skeletal review to assess the patient's spine, hip, and skull, and address any concerns.
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to support the patient's development and address any behavioral differences.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural issue with his heart, which was identified by doctors. The specifics and severity of this issue are not fully understood by the parents.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes. Some may require surgery, while others only need monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has feeding difficulties, is very picky, and refuses certain textures or smells, making daily feeding a challenge.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds. A lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes stares off into space and doesn't respond for a few seconds, which has happened a handful of times. This could be indicative of seizure activity or other neurological issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments. In a small number of cases, epilepsy can be difficult to treat.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had otitis media last year, which was treated and cleared up. There are no current issues reported with the ears or nose.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss. Many children have required multiple grommet insertions to relieve pressure inside the ear, and some have still required hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sits too close to the TV and books, suggesting potential vision problems. The parents are concerned about his ability to see things unless they are right in front of him.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint. Treatment can include patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery to bring the eyes into line.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles with chewing harder foods like apples or meat, which could be related to his teeth or other issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel. Regular dental check-ups are important, especially for those with significant sensory issues.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school. The extra demands of mainstream secondary school may prove too challenging, and children may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP).

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety. Medication(s) may be appropriate in some circumstances.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was born with hip dysplasia and is awaiting the next steps in treatment.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis). Many people have short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly). A small number of children have had hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor for dental concerns such as weak enamel.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to check for conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess for vision problems such as astigmatism or squint.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor the structural heart issue.
* Skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess for any skeletal anomalies.
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental delays and behavioural differences.
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Regular monitoring for signs of tethered cord, especially if sacral dimple is present.

## 1) RESPIRATORY

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's heart needs regular check-ups to ensure everything stays okay, indicating a potential heart condition that requires monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is a slow gainer and eats very little, making meal times frustrating and causing concern about nutrient intake.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds, with a lack of interest in feeding being a significant and long-lasting issue in some cases.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an issue with his spinal cord that specialists are monitoring, which may affect his development or movement.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and some have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, and an unusual gait.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes does not respond to his name being called, suggesting potential hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, with many requiring multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble seeing things far away, needs to squint to read or watch TV, and may have myopia, necessitating glasses.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with treatment options including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth break or chip easily, requiring careful management during eating and play.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have large front teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns, necessitating regular dental check-ups and careful brushing.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically require extra help in school, with many attending mainstream primary school but potentially transferring to special schooling or requiring Educational Health Care Plans due to the challenges of mainstream secondary school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often exhibit developmental delay, behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may benefit from medication, physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has noticeably different posture when standing or walking, which is being addressed through physical therapy to strengthen muscles and improve balance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curved fingers, hip dysplasia, and an increased curvature of the spine, with some experiencing delayed closure of the soft spot on the head.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and address any issues promptly.
* Regular hearing reviews, particularly in the first few years, to identify and manage any hearing loss.
* Eyesight review to assess vision problems and prescribe corrective measures such as glasses.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, following diagnosis to monitor heart health.
* Consideration of a skeletal review, including X-rays of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to identify any skeletal anomalies.
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support development and address specific challenges.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient's breathing gets really fast when playing, which could be related to a heart condition, and requires further investigation.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced feeding difficulties, with a lack of interest in feeding and slow eating.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient took longer to learn how to walk and sit than other kids, indicating a potential neurological delay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and developmental delay is common.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had glue ear, which was treated, and may be at risk for recurrence.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia (nearsightedness) and is waiting for glasses to correct it.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

We've noticed this issue for a while now, and it seems to affect his ability to follow lessons comfortably. He often squints or leans forward to get a better view.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: There are times when our child doesn't respond immediately when called. It's as if he didn't hear us, even when we're standing right next to him. This has happened both at home and in quieter environments, so we're concerned it might be related to his hearing.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: His teeth seem to break or chip very easily. Even minor accidents, like biting into something hard or a slight knock against another tooth, can cause damage. We've had to take him to the dentist more frequently than usual because of this issue.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Yes, our child was born with a septal defect. We've been working closely with cardiologists to monitor the condition and ensure it doesn't worsen over time. So far, the treatments and lifestyle adjustments have helped manage the issue effectively.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Our child gets tired quickly during physical activity. Simple tasks like playing outside or running around with friends can leave him exhausted sooner than his peers. This has been noticeable since he started engaging in more active play.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Our child has a feeding aversion. Certain textures or smells of food can put him off completely. Mealtime can be challenging, and we've had to work with him to find foods he's comfortable eating.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: In addition to the issues already mentioned, our child seems behind other children in development. His fontanelle also took longer to close than typical, which was another concern we've been monitoring. These developmental delays and physical differences have required us to adapt his education and activities to better suit his needs.
report:
# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was born with a septal defect, which has been managed with treatments and lifestyle adjustments under the guidance of cardiologists.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, some of which may require surgery or monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a feeding aversion with certain textures or smells of food, making mealtime challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds. A very small number of children have required longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired quickly during physical activity and has developmental delays, including a slower closure of the fontanelle.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments. Developmental delay is common, ranging from mild to severe, and can include delays in rolling, sitting, walking, and other milestones.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing issues, as indicated by not responding immediately when called, even in quiet environments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss. Many children require multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles to see the board at school, especially with small letters or from a distance, and often squints or leans forward to get a better view.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint. Regular eyesight reviews are recommended.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth break or chip very easily, requiring more frequent dental visits.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome, and careful brushing is very important. Regular dental check-ups are recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's developmental delays and physical differences have required adaptations in his education and activities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP).

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays and gets tired quickly during physical activity.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety. Developmental delay is common, and the degree of delay ranges from mild to severe.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's fontanelle took longer to close than typical.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis). Many have short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and address any issues promptly.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5, even if earlier reviews give a clear response, to monitor for any signs of hearing loss.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess for vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, following diagnosis to assess heart condition.
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) in children following diagnosis to monitor for any skeletal anomalies.
* Monitor growth velocity, and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental needs.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has concerns with her heart that require regular check-ups with a cardiologist to monitor her condition.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experienced feeding difficulties as a baby, including spitting up and trouble latching on, but this seems to have passed.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems a bit clumsy compared to other kids her age, with issues such as tripping over her own feet, and has been noted to have coordination issues that require monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing issues, such as tuning out certain sounds or voices, especially with background noise, and may need help with this.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, and many require multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient rubs her eyes a lot, especially when trying to focus, which may indicate a vision problem.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, which can be treated with patching, exercises, glasses, or surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains about tooth sensitivity, especially with cold foods, which has been an issue since she started eating solid foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups, with some needing specialist care.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is behind where she should be for her age developmentally and requires work at home to help catch her up.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with many attending mainstream primary school but possibly transferring to special schooling or requiring Educational Health Care Plans for secondary school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays and requires support to catch up.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may benefit from medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of their spinal bones, short fingers, and curvature of the 5th fingers, with a small number experiencing hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address tooth sensitivity and other dental concerns.
* Hearing reviews to age 5 to assess and address any hearing issues.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to evaluate and treat any vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart condition.
* Consideration of a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess for any skeletal anomalies.
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support developmental delays and behavioural differences.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences faster breathing rates than expected during moderate physical activity.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has been observed to breathe faster than expected during playtime, suggesting potential cardiac issues. 
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble digesting certain foods, leading to discomfort and occasional distress during meals.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences epileptic seizures, which are currently under control with medication.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had a glue ear in the past, which was treated with antibiotics, and currently has no recurring issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often squints when looking at things, particularly when trying to focus on something close up.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains of tooth sensitivity, specifically when eating cold foods or drinks.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have large front teeth and may experience weak enamel, making regular dental check-ups important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty articulating thoughts into coherent speech.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many go to mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curved fingers, and an increased curvature of the spine.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel weakness
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to check for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to assess for vision problems such as astigmatism or squint
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to assess for heart conditions
* Consider a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to assess for skeletal anomalies
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental delays and difficulties.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a valvular abnormality that requires further testing to understand its severity.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has issues with food textures, which makes mealtime challenging, and has trouble chewing harder foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypotonia, with muscles that seem too tight or stiff at times.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have neurological differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD) or ADHD.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble hearing and often turns up the volume on the TV.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble with her eyes, often rubbing them when trying to focus, and may have vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble chewing harder foods and may have dental concerns.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have large front teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns, and require regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP).

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hip dysplasia, which affects her hip joint, and is undergoing physical therapy.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, such as an unusual structure of their spinal bones, short fingers, or curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor dental concerns
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor hearing loss
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor vision problems
* Cardiac review to monitor heart condition
* Referral for a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to monitor skeletal anomalies
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support development and address challenges.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect that was discovered during a routine check-up. The doctors keep a close eye on it to ensure it doesn't cause any major issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient can be quite picky with food and often refuses to eat certain things due to sensory issues with textures. 
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was born with a tethered cord condition, which has been monitored by specialists to address any potential issues early on.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported as having seizures, of varying types, and some may have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tends to turn the TV volume up really high because he says it's hard for him to hear otherwise, indicating potential hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, which means he has trouble seeing things clearly unless they're really close up, and he uses glasses to help correct it.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak tooth enamel, and the parents make sure he brushes his teeth regularly and gently to avoid making it worse.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's astigmatism and hearing difficulties have been a challenge for him in school, especially during lessons where they show videos or write on the board.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school, and some may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has scoliosis, with his back curving slightly more than it should, and he sees a specialist regularly to monitor the progression and consider treatment options if necessary.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and may have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

* Regular eyesight reviews to monitor the patient's astigmatism and adjust treatment as necessary.
* Regular monitoring of the patient's scoliosis to consider treatment options if necessary.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation, which is managed with dietary changes and occasional medication.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures, which are being managed with medication and regular adjustments to treatment as needed.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had a glue ear in the past, which caused temporary hearing issues, but his hearing has returned to normal after treatment.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, which means he has difficulty seeing distant objects clearly, and is due for another assessment to monitor the progression.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has been experiencing tooth sensitivity, especially when eating cold foods, and has large front teeth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have weak enamel, and regular dental check-ups are recommended.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel weakness

* Regular monitoring of the patient's heart condition to ensure it does not impact daily life or activity levels

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired quickly when playing outside or running around, indicating potential cardiac issues that need monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, some of which may require surgery or monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has bowel problems, including accidents and struggles with going to the bathroom, requiring the development of good bowel habits and routines.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds, with a small number needing longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypotonia, affecting her muscle tone and making it harder for her to move around or support herself, and also exhibits developmental delays.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments, though in some cases, epilepsy can be difficult to treat.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes doesn't respond when called, suggesting potential hearing issues, and has myopia, affecting her ability to see distant objects clearly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, and many have speech delay, which may be linked to hearing concerns.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, indicating difficulty seeing objects at a distance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, which can be treated with patching, exercises, glasses, or surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth seem to break or chip easily, requiring careful management during eating and play.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Besides large front teeth, individuals with KBG syndrome can have weak enamel, making regular dental check-ups important, and some may experience other dental concerns.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is behind in development compared to her peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with most attending mainstream primary school but potentially transferring to special schooling or requiring Educational Health Care Plans for secondary school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental delays and moves differently compared to her peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapeutic interventions.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of spinal bones leading to increased curvature of the spine, short fingers, and curvature of the 5th fingers, with a small number experiencing hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and address any dental concerns.
* Hearing reviews up to age 5 to assess and address any hearing issues.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to correct any vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, following diagnosis to assess heart health.
* Consideration of a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) in children following diagnosis to identify any skeletal anomalies.
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support development and address specific challenges.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a known structural abnormality in his heart that is being monitored closely by a cardiologist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences discomfort after meals and has trouble eating certain foods, making meal times challenging and requiring careful diet management.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds, with a small number needing longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences hypotonia, affecting his muscle tone, and has speech development issues, not talking as much as expected for his age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and many have developmental delay, with the degree ranging from mild to severe.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems to have inconsistent hearing, sometimes missing out on loud and clear sounds without a specific pattern.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, with many requiring multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sits very close to the TV and books, suggesting potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with treatment including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs frequent dental visits due to various issues, indicating challenges with dental care.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel, requiring careful brushing and regular dental check-ups, especially with a specialist SEN dentist for those with significant sensory issues.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's speech development issues and potential vision problems may impact his educational progress.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with many attending mainstream primary school but potentially transferring to special schooling or requiring Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP) for secondary school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has speech development issues and potential behavioral concerns related to his developmental delays.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, with medication sometimes being appropriate.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of spinal bones leading to scoliosis, delayed closure of the soft spot on the head, short fingers (brachydactyly), and curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to address dental care challenges.
* Hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess for vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor the known heart structural abnormality.
* Consideration for a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess for skeletal anomalies.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental delays and speech development issues.
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with consideration for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Regular monitoring by a cardiologist for the heart condition.
* Management of feeding difficulties and dietary challenges.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.

Parent: He's been complaining about tooth sensitivity, especially when eating cold foods like ice cream or cold drinks. It seems to really bother him, and he tries to avoid those things now.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: I've observed that he gets tired more quickly than other kids his age. We went to the park last weekend, and after just a couple of hours of playing, he was exhausted and wanted to go home.

Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Developmentally, he's been a bit slower than his peers. For example, he took longer to learn how to walk or sit up compared to other children. 

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: He's had constipation issues for a while now. We've tried changing his diet a bit and encouraging more fluids, but it's still a problem.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Actually, yes. He was diagnosed with hip dysplasia, and we're currently undergoing treatment for that. The doctors are monitoring it closely to ensure everything develops correctly.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular heart check-ups as a precautionary measure. The cardiologist keeps a close eye on her condition to ensure everything remains stable.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: Mealtime can be challenging for her. She's picky about what she eats, and some foods seem to disagree with her. 
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems a bit clumsier than her peers. Her coordination and balance could be better, and the parents are considering enrolling her in activities that might help improve these skills. She also struggles to express herself effectively, which leads to frustration for both her and her parents.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people are reported as having seizures, of varying types. Seizures typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tends to get overwhelmed in noisy environments, like playgrounds or crowded restaurants. It's not that she can't hear, but more that the noise levels her out.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has mentioned a few times that she can't see the board clearly at school, and it frustrates her. The parents are planning to get her eyes checked to rule out any potential issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, and short- or long sightedness.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs to visit the dentist quite frequently due to cavities and tooth decay. The parents are working on improving her oral hygiene routine to reduce these visits.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns. Weak enamel is frequently seen, and careful brushing is very important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's difficulty articulating her thoughts and needs leads to frustration for both her and her parents. They are seeking ways to support her communication development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems a bit clumsier than her peers. Her coordination and balance could be better, and the parents are considering enrolling her in activities that might help improve these skills.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine. Many people with KBG syndrome have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and prevent cavities and tooth decay.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for any hearing loss or issues.
* Eyesight review to rule out any potential vision problems.
* Cardiac review to monitor heart condition and ensure stability.
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support development and address challenges.
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty keeping up with physical activities and gets winded easily, suggesting potential cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences feeding aversion and has difficulty with certain foods, making mealtime challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences frequent falls, suggesting potential issues with coordination and balance, and has slower language development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and some have developmental delay and learning difficulties.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often asks for repetitions of what was said, indicating potential hearing or understanding difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient rubs her eyes frequently, especially when trying to focus, suggesting potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth are fragile and prone to breaking or chipping easily.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's language development is slower than expected, with limited vocabulary at three years old.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome often require extra help in school and may need to transfer to special schooling or have Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences feeding aversion and has slower language development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences frequent falls, suggesting potential issues with coordination and balance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, such as an unusual structure of their spinal bones, short fingers, or hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and prevent dental issues.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to detect any potential hearing problems.
* Eyesight review to assess vision and potential need for corrective measures.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to evaluate heart health.
* Consideration of a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to assess bone health and potential skeletal anomalies.
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental needs.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural abnormality with his heart that requires close monitoring to prevent it from becoming more serious over time.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had feeding difficulties as a baby, including trouble latching on and spitting up, but this has mostly resolved.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired quickly during physical activity and has difficulty with balance and coordination, often tripping over his own feet.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and some may have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often asks people to repeat themselves, suggesting hearing difficulties, and has required frequent dental check-ups due to prone teeth problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, and many have speech delay.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often squints when looking at things, especially in bright light, indicating potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with some requiring patching, exercises, glasses, or surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has prone teeth problems, requiring frequent dental check-ups to monitor for cavities and plaque build-up.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have weak enamel and require regular dental check-ups, with some having significant dental concerns.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with many attending mainstream primary school but potentially transferring to special schooling or requiring Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hip dysplasia, which is being managed with physiotherapy, and experiences difficulties with balance and coordination.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curved fingers, and an increased curvature of the spine, with a small number having hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor for cavities and plaque build-up
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor the structural heart abnormality
* Physiotherapy to manage hip dysplasia and balance difficulties
* Consideration of occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental needs

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient breathes faster during play than expected.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has faster breathing during play, and the parent has concerns about the child's heart rate.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is very picky with food textures and has difficulty eating certain foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has epilepsy, which is managed with medication and regular check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient turns the volume of the TV very high, suggesting possible hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sits very close to the TV or books, suggesting possible vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth break or chip easily.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have weak enamel, and careful brushing is very important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems behind other children in development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many go to mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems behind other children in development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, and the degree of delay ranges from mild to severe.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has scoliosis.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and some have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and prevent enamel weakness
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to monitor for vision problems
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor for heart conditions
* Skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to monitor for skeletal abnormalities
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental delay and other needs
* Monitoring of growth velocity and referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consideration of review and investigation for tethered cord if clinical concerns arise

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural issue with his heart that was identified during a routine check-up. So far, it hasn't caused significant problems in daily life, but it is monitored closely.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient shows a strong aversion to certain foods and textures, and feeding has been challenging. Sometimes meals end in tantrums if he's presented with something new or unappealing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds. A very small number of children have required longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures occasionally, which are under control with medication. He also has delayed speech development, taking longer to articulate thoughts and form coherent sentences compared to peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments. Developmental delay has been reported in almost all children with KBG syndrome, ranging from mild to severe.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often asks people to repeat themselves because he didn't catch what they said the first time, indicating potential hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss. Many children have required multiple aeration tube (grommet) insertions to relieve pressure inside the ear.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tends to sit very close to the TV or when reading books, which makes his parents worry about his eyesight.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint. Treatment can include patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery to bring the eyes into line.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has noticeably larger front teeth than usual, which might be related to his jaw alignment or bite.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's delayed speech development and potential hearing difficulties may impact his educational progress.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school. The extra demands of mainstream secondary school may prove too challenging, and children may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP).

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tantrums during meals when presented with new or unappealing foods, and has delayed speech development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety. Medication(s) may be appropriate in some circumstances.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: There is an ongoing investigation into some undescended test results that require further examination.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis). Many people with KBG syndrome have short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor the patient's dental health and address any concerns related to his large front teeth.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor the patient's hearing and address any concerns related to potential hearing loss.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess the patient's vision and address any concerns related to his eyesight.
* Cardiac review to monitor the patient's heart condition and adjust treatment as necessary.
* Neurological monitoring to manage the patient's seizures and adjust medication as necessary.
* Speech therapy to support the patient's speech development and address any concerns related to his delayed speech.
* Occupational therapy to support the patient's fine motor skills and address any concerns related to his feeding difficulties.
* Behavioural therapy to support the patient's behavioural development and address any concerns related to his tantrums and mealtime challenges.
