# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a heart valve issue that requires regular check-ups to ensure everything is okay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is picky about what he eats and some foods with weird textures make him not want to eat them.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has seizures sometimes and has to take medicine to manage them.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often asks people to repeat what they said because he didn't hear it right the first time, and he has issues with his palate.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss, and some have subtler anomalies of the palate.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient rubs his eyes a lot when he's trying to focus, especially when reading or watching TV.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has big front teeth, and the dentist has advised to keep an eye on them.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, people with KBG syndrome can have weak enamel and other dental concerns, making regular dental check-ups important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's forehead didn't close right when he was a baby, and there are issues with how his heart formed.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and some have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor the patient's teeth
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to check for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to check for vision problems
* Cardiac review to monitor the patient's heart valve issue
* Consider a palate review to address feeding and speech concerns
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support the patient's development and behaviour.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired more easily than his peers, which may indicate a potential cardiac issue that needs monitoring to ensure it doesn't impact his ability to participate fully in physical activities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, which may require surgery or monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient can be quite picky about food and will often refuse to eat certain items, leading to concerns about whether he's getting a balanced diet and all the necessary nutrients for growth and development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds. A very small number of children have required longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient falls more often than other kids his age, which could be due to clumsiness or possibly something more serious that needs to be investigated further, and he struggles with clarity when trying to express himself verbally.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported as having seizures, of varying types, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes doesn't immediately respond when called, as if he hasn't heard or is too engrossed in whatever he's doing to notice, and this happens frequently enough to disrupt daily interactions.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss, and many children have required multiple aeration tube insertions to relieve pressure inside the ear.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tendency to squint, which can make it difficult for him to see things clearly, especially when looking at distant objects or reading from the board in class.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint, which can be treated with patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs to visit the dentist quite often due to high sugar content in his diet and poor oral hygiene practices when he was younger, and the dentist has mentioned that his teeth are prone to cavities and other issues if not properly cared for.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome, and careful brushing is very important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's communication skills are affected as he struggles with clarity when trying to express himself verbally.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school, and the extra demands of mainstream secondary school may prove too challenging.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays and learning difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and developmental delay has been reported in almost all children with KBG syndrome.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hip dysplasia which requires regular check-ups to ensure proper development and prevent future complications.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many people have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and prevent dental issues.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to address any hearing concerns.
* Eyesight review to assess and treat any vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to investigate potential heart conditions.
* Skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to monitor bone development and detect any skeletal anomalies.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support the patient's development and address any delays or difficulties.
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Regular check-ups for hip dysplasia to ensure proper development and prevent future complications.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired more easily than other kids her age and needs to sit down and rest after a while, suggesting possible cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is fussy about the texture of foods and has difficulty eating certain foods, making mealtime challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient falls more often than her friends, suggesting balance issues, and has difficulty with speech, as her words get jumbled up.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may experience developmental delay and behavioral differences.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had a glue ear recently and has difficulty hearing, which has been treated.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient squints a lot, which can make her eyes get really tired, and has difficulty focusing on things that are far away.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak enamel and needs to brush her teeth more regularly and use a special toothpaste.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty with speech and balance, and may have behavioral differences.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curved fingers, and hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth enamel and overall dental health.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight review to monitor for vision problems such as astigmatism and squint.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor for heart conditions.
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to address developmental delays and behavioral differences.
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient had a glue ear recently and frequently rubs her eyes, especially when she's trying to focus on something.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

report:
# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs to go back to the cardiologist regularly for check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is sometimes very picky about food and will refuse to eat certain things, and has feeding difficulties with tough foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets very tired after playing outside for even short periods and has delayed developmental milestones.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some have developmental delay ranging from mild to severe.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had fluid in her ear once and needs regular hearing reviews.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often squints when trying to focus on things, and her eyes get tired easily.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulties with chewing and has trouble with tough foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have weak enamel, and some have large front teeth and other dental concerns.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is taking a bit longer than average to hit some developmental milestones.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has delayed developmental milestones and gets tired easily.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has noticeable posture issues when standing or walking.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and some have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor teeth and chewing difficulties
* Regular hearing reviews to monitor hearing loss and address any concerns
* Eyesight review to assess vision problems and address any concerns
* Cardiac review to monitor heart condition and address any concerns
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to address developmental delays and behavioural differences
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consider review and investigation for tethered cord if clinical concerns arise

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and may require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient falls more than other kids her age, and has developmental delays, including speech delay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and some may have developmental delays and learning difficulties.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing difficulties and asks to have things repeated often.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient squints and has trouble focusing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth break or chip easily.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may have weak enamel, large front teeth, and other dental concerns, making regular dental check-ups important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays and may require extra support in school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome often require extra help in school and may need to attend special schooling or have Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays, including speech delay, and moves differently than her peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, such as an unusual structure of the spinal bones, short fingers, or hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and prevent dental concerns.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor hearing and address any concerns.
* Eyesight review to assess vision and address any concerns.
* Cardiac review to monitor heart health and address any concerns.
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to support developmental delays and behavioral differences.
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
